actions.description: Move the motor to a target in its configured unit: send MoveMotor, then poll fresh GetMotorFull state until Move Complete. Completed means the server reported Move Complete, not that the target was reached: a MoveMotor the server refuses is swallowed upstream and also ends completed; compare position with the target

inputs.description: Target in the motor's configured unit (the BCS configuration's Units), which the clone does not state; MHS requires a unit on a numeric input, and 1 stands for that unknown configured unit
inputs.name: target_position

actions.name: move

outputs.description: The target that was sent, in the configured unit
outputs.name: target_position

outputs.description: Fresh Raw Motor Position observed when the move completed
outputs.name: position

outputs.description: The fresh Motor State -> Move Complete at the last poll
outputs.name: move_complete

actions.description: Stop the motor: send the native StopMotor command, then require two consecutive fresh GetMotorFull reports of Move Complete before reporting stopped
actions.name: stop_motion

outputs.description: True only after two consecutive fresh Move Complete reports
outputs.name: stopped

outputs.description: Fresh Raw Motor Position observed when the stop was confirmed
outputs.name: position

device.model: BCSMotor over the BCS ZeroMQ server
device.name: BCS motor (bcsophyd.zmq.bcs_motor.BCSMotor)

facts.text: BCSMotor is an Ophyd Device and PositionerBase for one motor controlled through the BCS ZeroMQ server
BCSMotor's constructor reads name, originalName, itemType, prefix, units, bridgeIP, bridgePort, timeout and settle_time from its keyword arguments and creates a BCSServer
move() sets moveComplete=False and isMoving=True, sends zmq_move_motor([originalName], [new_position]) and starts a monitor thread
monitor_motor_status polls update() every check_interval=0.1 s and declares the move finished when moveComplete is true; the computed distance to the target is logged but not used
stop() sends zmq_stop_motor([originalName]) and sets isMoving=False; it does not set moveComplete
read() calls zmq_get_motor_full_async(originalName), stores the first data element's 'Raw Motor Position' in _position and returns it as a value with a timestamp under the motor name
The constructor creates self._lock to prevent concurrent access to the ZeroMQ server
None of the ZeroMQ wrappers acquires self._lock
update() calls zmq_get_motor_full(originalName) and reads data[0]['Motor State']['Move Complete'] and data[0]['Raw Motor Position']; it catches and logs every exception without re-raising
zmq_move_motor runs asyncio.run(_zmq_move_motor_async(...)) in a new Thread, joins it and returns nothing; it checks no result
_zmq_move_motor_async raises when the MoveMotor reply is unsuccessful or lists the motor as not found or timed out
zmq_stop_motor runs asyncio.run(_zmq_stop_motor_async(...)) in a new Thread, joins it and returns nothing; it checks no result
_zmq_stop_motor_async raises only when the StopMotor reply success is false; it does not check the timed_out or not_found lists
zmq_get_motor_full raises RuntimeError when the worker thread produced no result, so a failed GetMotorFull is visible to the caller
zmq_get_motor_full_async raises RuntimeError when the response success is false
parse_get_motor_full raises ValueError when the reply success is false or the data field is empty
move_motor sends the MoveMotor request and documents timed_out and not_found lists in the reply
stop_motor sends the StopMotor request; its documentation says the stop command is immediately sent to the motor controller, and timed_out means the command queue is unavailable
get_motor_full sends the GetMotorFull request and returns a data list of state dictionaries
MotorStatus is a Flag enum of status bits (HOME=1 through MOVE_LT_THRESHOLD=131072); FORWARD_LIMIT, REVERSE_LIMIT and the RAW_*_LIMIT members are bit flags, not position bounds
bcs_request sends the JSON request on self._zmq_socket and awaits the reply; the method sets no receive timeout
connect() fetches the server public key, configures CURVE keys and connects the REQ socket to port+1
The device manager builds the selected motor class through Happi with device_class='bcsophyd.zmq.bcs_motor.BCSMotor'
The device manager takes the motor's unit from the BCS configuration's General Parameters -> Units and also records Forward SW Limit (Units) and Reverse SW Limit (Units) in the Happi item
The device manager reads the motor parameter Stop Decel (c/s^2) into a stop_decel field
BCSMotor's constructor reads no travel limit: its settings are name, originalName, itemType, prefix, units, bridgeIP, bridgePort, timeout and settle_time
check_server_connection calls sys.exit(1) when the BCS server check returns false
BCSAreaDetector's image is one of three hard-coded 3x3 patterns and acquire_frame puts that pattern into the Signal, so it is a test pattern device rather than a camera read
The README describes BCSAreaDetector as '2D detector support (under development)'

measures.description: Raw motor position from a fresh GetMotorFull, in the motor's configured unit (the BCS configuration's General Parameters -> Units; the driver does not convert)
measures.name: position

measures.description: True unless the fresh GetMotorFull state reports Motor State -> Move Complete
measures.name: moving

measures.description: The unit string the deployment passed to the factory (BCSMotor keeps it as given); BCSDeviceManager would take it from the BCS configuration's General Parameters -> Units
measures.name: units

operator_required.name: move
operator_required.reason: the clone states no travel range for a configured motor: the BCS configuration supplies the unit, forward and reverse software limits, and they are not carried by BCSMotor; the site must supply this motor's range before any move

safe_state.description: No safe state is certified: the e-stop sends StopMotor and the stop action requires two fresh Move Complete reports, but StopMotor shares one REQ socket with the reads and moves, so an e-stop that cancels a move waiting for a GetMotorFull reply leaves the socket refusing every request: StopMotor never arrives and the motor finishes its commanded move; the e-stop reports SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held
